title: Why do journalists use Signal and how to protect sources on Mac
metaTitle: Why do journalists use Signal: Source protection guide for Mac users
description: Learn why do journalists use Signal for secure communication and how to protect sensitive sources on your Mac without complex tools.
intro: Journalists use Signal because it offers robust, end-to-end encryption that keeps communications private from third parties, including service providers and government entities. Protecting your sources is a fundamental duty, but the technical burden can feel overwhelming when you are working against a deadline.
tldr: Signal provides end-to-end encryption for messages and calls.
Enable FileVault on your Mac to secure your local drive.
Use local-first apps like Obsidian to keep research off the cloud.
Practice consistent operational security to minimize your digital footprint.
Lazur helps you manage your security workflow by answering questions about settings and shortcuts.

blocks.text: Why do journalists use Signal and other secure tools

Signal is the standard for journalists because it uses the Signal Protocol to ensure that only the sender and recipient can read messages. Unlike standard SMS or unencrypted chat apps, Signal does not store your message history on their servers. This means if a provider receives a subpoena, they have no content to hand over. For a reporter, this creates a necessary layer of separation between your investigative work and potential legal discovery.
The costs of failing to protect sources

The primary cost is the loss of trust. If a source believes their identity or information is at risk, they will stop talking to you. This kills stories before they start. Beyond the professional impact, there is a significant personal cost. Journalists who are subpoenaed face immense financial strain from legal fees and the persistent stress of fighting to protect their notes. This contributes to the burnout crisis, where over 80 percent of journalists report chronic stress.

Security failures rarely come from a single hack. They usually stem from convenience. When you are on a deadline, you might send a sensitive document via standard email or save notes in a cloud app that scans your content. Sophisticated spyware like Pegasus can also bypass traditional defenses by turning your device into a monitoring tool. The gap between the complexity of security tools and the speed required in a newsroom leads many reporters to take shortcuts.

items: Enable FileVault: Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > FileVault. This encrypts your entire hard drive so your data is unreadable if your Mac is stolen.
Use local-first notes: Apps like Obsidian store files on your Mac, not on a remote server. You can keep your research in a folder that you control.
Secure your passwords: Use a password manager like 1Password or the built-in iCloud Keychain to ensure every account has a unique, complex password.
Use encrypted email: ProtonMail provides end-to-end encryption for communications and is based in Switzerland, which has strong privacy laws.
Keep your system updated: Always click Install when macOS prompts for a security update. These updates often patch vulnerabilities that could expose your data.

blocks.text: If you work for a large organization, always check your IT department's policy on encryption and third-party tools. Some newsrooms have specific software they require you to use for sensitive communications.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps with your security workflow

Lazur acts as a bridge between your security needs and your daily tasks. You do not need to hunt through menus to find privacy settings. You can hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where a specific setting is located. It will point to the exact toggle in your System Settings. This saves time and helps you maintain your security posture without breaking your flow.

faq.question: Is Signal safe for all my communications?
faq.answer: Signal is highly secure for text and calls, but it cannot protect you if your device itself is compromised by advanced spyware. Always keep your Mac and apps updated.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my sensitive notes?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not store your screen content or audio. It only processes information while you hold the activation key. Your data remains on your Mac.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to encrypt my files?
faq.answer: Lazur does not perform file encryption. It can guide you to the correct system tools like FileVault or help you find where to set up encrypted containers using tools like VeraCrypt.

costs.title: Loss of source trust
costs.text: If you fail to protect a source, they will stop talking to you, which ends your ability to report on sensitive topics.

costs.title: Legal and financial risk
costs.text: Subpoenas require legal counsel and time, which can drain your resources and pull you away from your reporting duties.

costs.title: Mental health strain
costs.text: The constant need to manage security protocols while meeting deadlines contributes significantly to burnout.

causes.title: Workflow pressure
causes.text: Deadlines often force journalists to choose speed over security, leading them to use less secure channels.

causes.title: Tool complexity
causes.text: High-security tools are often difficult to configure, making it easier to skip them entirely.

causes.title: Advanced surveillance
causes.text: Sophisticated spyware can bypass common security measures, creating a false sense of safety.

fixes.title: Enable FileVault
fixes.text: Navigate to System Settings > Privacy & Security > FileVault to encrypt your drive.

fixes.title: Adopt local-first apps
fixes.text: Use applications like Obsidian that store data on your machine rather than in the cloud.

fixes.title: Use Signal for communication
fixes.text: Switch to Signal for all sensitive conversations to leverage end-to-end encryption.
